ledger.note: 58-52 BC: the Cherusci are first attested in Caesar's Gallic War, which says the Bacenis Forest protected the Suebi from them. The date is the first record (the range 58-52 BC), not a founding; the land is the page's middle Weser.

Cherusci page: 'In 8 BC Augustus and future emperor Tiberius, the brother of Drusus, came north' and 'Roman writers thereafter treated the Cherusci as a dependent and ostensibly friendly people'; Germanic Wars page: '12-9 BC ... Cherusci, Marsi and Sicambri subdued'. The terms are unknown and the page does not use 'client' or 'vassal'; the year is the page's, the status and the shape are the reading (confidence 2). ledger.note: 14: Germanicus's reprisals begin. '14-16 AD: Germanicus runs reprisal campaigns with mixed success'; in 15 he rescues Segestes and in 16 he fights Arminius at Idistaviso and the Angrivarian Wall. The Germanic Wars page has '14-16: Roman retaliation against Cherusci, Chatti, Bructeri and Marsi'. 9 AD's victory over Varus, which drove Rome from the land east of the Rhine, is not given a dated gain here because the Roman province of Germania ('Varus governs the new province of Germania', 6-7 AD) has no region name.

wars.name: Drusus's campaigns in Germania
wars.outcome: Drusus reached the Weser in 11 BC but turned back; in 9 BC he defeated an alliance of Sicambri, Cherusci and Suebi and died at the end of the campaign; in 8 BC the Cherusci's submission left them a dependent, friendly people.
wars.note: Terms of the 8 BC submission unknown.

wars.name: Battle of the Teutoburg Forest and Germanicus's campaigns

zones.text: 'around the middle of the Weser River', with the Angrivarii to the north and the Chatti to the southwest (a radius round Hameln and Minden, which the gazetteer lacks)
the Teutoburg Forest, where Arminius's coalition ambushed three legions in 9 (the gazetteer has no such name; Osnabrück stands at the north-western end of the ridge)

wars.outcome: In 9 AD Arminius's coalition destroyed three Roman legions under Varus; in 14-16 Germanicus ran reprisals with mixed success (Idistaviso, the Angrivarian Wall) and was recalled; the Cherusci were not destroyed.
wars.note: Tiberius had re-subjugated the Cherusci in 4-5 AD and crossed the Weser.

wars.name: War between Arminius and Maroboduus
wars.outcome: A Cheruscan faction under Inguiomerus defected to Maroboduus in 17 AD (Cherusci page); the marcomanni dossier has the war of the two coalitions in 17 and Maroboduus's fall in 19. Arminius was killed by relatives in 21.
wars.note: Italicus was asked for as chieftain in 47, later expelled and reinstalled by the Langobardi.
